title: Strike Fighter Tactics Instructor (I) (Col to 2ndLt) NMOS (7518, 7523, 7525, 8042), DC AVN
raw_text:
27. MOS 7542, Strike Fighter Tactics Instructor (I) (Col to 2ndLt) NMOS
(7518, 7523, 7525, 8042), DC AVN

    a. Summary. Strike Fighter Tactics Instructors (SFTI) train aviation
personnel on advanced tactics techniques and procedures (TTPs) across all
combat missions at the individual unit and integrated air wing levels in a
total threat environment in coordination with ground and other aviation
units.   This MOS will be assigned only as a Necessary MOS to qualified
aviation personnel.

    b. Prerequisites.       Security requirement:   top secret security clearance
eligibility.

    c. Requirements. Complete the TOPGUN Strike Fighter Tactics Instructor
(SFTI) Course (N39KYB1).

       d.   Duties

        (1) Provides air support by electronic countermeasures against enemy
fighters, ground radars, communications networks, and radar controlled guns
during strikes against enemy installations; provides air defense by active
and passive electronic countermeasures against enemy aircraft and provides
airborne early warning; provides aerial intelligence by electronic mapping,
reconnaissance, and early warning; supervises development of intelligence
obtained; and plans and executes photographic missions over assigned areas to
photograph terrain and installations.

        (2) Supervises developing, printing, and assembling of aerial
photographs and mosaics.




                                         1-289                        Enclosure (1)
 1143                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



            (3) Executes offensive and defensive fighter tactics.

            (4) Operates from carrier and land bases.

            (5) Commands or may assist in commanding an aviation unit.

        (6) Upon meeting all eligibility listed for the certification of this
MOS, the individual recipient shall coordinate with their unit administration
department to ensure this MOS is added to their Official Military Personnel
File (OMPF) in order to accurately reflect the corresponding aviation
qualification/designation within their permanent record.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Airline Pilots, Copilots, and Flight Engineers 53-2011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

matches: Instruct other pilots and student pilots in aircraft operations.

Strike Fighter Tactics Instructors (SFTI) train aviation personnel on advanced tactics techniques and procedures (TTPs) across all combat missions at the individual unit and integrated air wing levels in a total threat environment in coordination with ground and other aviation units.
Use airfield landing and navigational aids and digital data terminal communications equipment to perform duties.
d. Duties (1) Provides air support by electronic countermeasures against enemy fighters, ground radars, communications networks, and radar controlled guns during strikes against enemy installations.
Monitor aircraft within a specific airspace, using radar, computer equipment, or visual references.
provides air defense by active and passive electronic countermeasures against enemy aircraft and provides airborne early warning.
Gather and evaluate information, using tools such as aerial photographs, radar equipment, or sensitive radio equipment.
provides aerial intelligence by electronic mapping, reconnaissance, and early warning.
Supervise, evaluate, or refer instructors to skill development classes.
Set up, mount, or install photographic equipment and cameras.
and plans and executes photographic missions over assigned areas to photograph terrain and installations.
Supervise or coordinate activities of workers engaged in surveying, plotting data, drafting maps, or producing blueprints, photostats, or photographs.
(2) Supervises developing, printing, and assembling of aerial photographs and mosaics.
Develop defense plans or tactics, using intelligence and other information.
(3) Executes offensive and defensive fighter tactics.
Maintain air-to-ground and point-to-point radio contact with aircraft commanders.
(5) Commands or may assist in commanding an aviation unit.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
